import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Calculate total spending for each customer
df['Total_Spending'] = (df['MntWines'] + df['MntFruits'] + df['MntMeatProducts'] + 
                        df['MntFishProducts'] + df['MntSweetProducts'] + df['MntGoldProds'])

# Categorize income into bins
income_bins = [0, 30000, 60000, 90000, 120000, df['Income'].max()]
income_labels = ['<30k', '30k-60k', '60k-90k', '90k-120k', '>120k']
df['Income_Category'] = pd.cut(df['Income'], bins=income_bins, labels=income_labels, include_lowest=True)

# Plot a boxplot of total spending by income category
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.boxplot(x='Income_Category', y='Total_Spending', data=df, palette='Set3')

# Set plot title and labels
plt.title('Total Spending by Income Category', fontsize=14)
plt.xlabel('Income Category', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
